title: .NET 11 : ASP.NET Core: Union Type Support, OpenAPI 3.2 by Default and Blazor AI Components
gist: Microsoft shipped ASP.NET Core in .NET 11, a two-year Standard Term Support release adding C# 15 union types in JSON bodies, OpenAPI 3.2 by default, SignalR auth refresh, extensive Blazor static-SSR features, and an experimental Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI package for chat and agent UIs. Kestrel's parser change reportedly lifts throughput 20-40% under heavy invalid traffic.

insights.claim: Microsoft's .NET 11 is a Standard Term Support release with two years of support, shipping ASP.NET Core updates across Minimal APIs, OpenAPI, SignalR, Blazor, authentication and Kestrel.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Enterprises on long-term-support .NET versions may skip this release; STS limits adoption urgency.
insights.locator: Last week, Microsoft shipped ASP.NET Core in .NET 11

insights.claim: ASP.NET Core in .NET 11 generates OpenAPI 3.2 documents by default via Microsoft.OpenApi 3.3.1, a change Microsoft labels breaking, adding schemas for server-sent events, anyOf for unions and the HTTP QUERY method.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: API tooling vendors that lag OpenAPI 3.2 support face compatibility friction with .NET 11 users.
insights.locator: Developers who generate OpenAPI documents now get version 3.2

insights.claim: C# 15 union types can be used in JSON request and response bodies in Minimal APIs and MVC, but not for route, query, header or form binding.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Incremental language-level modernization keeps .NET competitive with TypeScript-style type systems for API development.
insights.locator: On the API side, developers can now use C# 15 union types

insights.claim: Microsoft added Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.AI, a set of Blazor components for chat and agent interfaces, but treats it as experimental and will keep it in prerelease throughout .NET 11.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Microsoft is embedding agent UI primitives into its web stack, but the prerelease status signals caution about production readiness.
insights.locator: The release notes flag this as a CSS breaking change

insights.claim: Kestrel's HTTP/1.1 parser no longer throws exceptions on malformed requests, reportedly raising throughput by up to 20 to 40 percent under heavy invalid traffic.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Improves resilience of .NET-hosted services under abusive or malformed traffic, lowering infrastructure cost for such loads.
insights.locator: Kestrel's HTTP/1.1 parser no longer throws exceptions

insights.claim: Blazor Interactive Server apps can opt in to pausing the circuit of a hidden browser tab after a delay (two minutes by default) to free server memory, alongside a new CacheView component for caching rendered markup.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Targets the server-memory cost that has been a scaling concern for stateful server-rendered Blazor apps.
insights.locator: For Interactive Server apps, an opt-in package

insights.claim: ASP.NET Core in .NET 11 adds SignalR authentication refresh for long-lived connections, an experimental Device Bound Session Credentials package tying session refresh to a browser-held private key, and default-on Zstandard compression.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Signals platform-level adoption of device-bound session security and Zstandard as defaults across the web stack.
insights.locator: On the security and server side, an experimental package
